body.en: A statement (proposition) is a sentence that is either true or false, but not both. Commands, questions, exclamations and opinions are not *statements*; nor are sentences with an unknown, like "x + 3 = 7", until x is fixed. Sentences with time words ("today", "here") may be statements only once the context is fixed. We name statements p, q, r.

points.en: Not: orders, questions, opinions, open sentences

body.en: The *negation* of p, written ~p, says "it is not the case that p"; it is true exactly when p is false. Care is needed with quantities: the negation of "All A are B" is "Some (at least one) A is not B", and the negation of "Some A is B" is "No A is B" (every A is not B). Negating twice returns the original: ~(~p) has the truth value of p.

problem.en: Write the negation of each: (a) Chennai is the capital of Tamil Nadu. (b) Every natural number is greater than 0. (c) There is a complex number that is not real.

steps.en: (a) Chennai is not the capital of Tamil Nadu.
(b) There is at least one natural number that is not greater than 0.

answer.en: See the steps; (a) false, (b) false, (c) false

a Chennai is not the capital of Tamil Nadu.

c Every complex number is real.

body.en: To negate a quantified statement, swap "all" ↔ "some" and flip the property: not(all A are B) = some A is not B; not(some A is B) = all A are not B.

narration.en: Swap and flip. To negate a quantified statement, swap "all" ↔ "some" and flip the property: not(all A are B) = some A is not B; not(some A is B) = all A are not B.

mnemonic.en: Swap the quantifier, flip the property.

say.en: Swap and flip. To negate a quantified statement, swap "all" ↔ "some" and flip the property: notall A are B equals some A is not B; notsome A is B equals all A are not B.
